title: Inbound call after furnace line 2 outage
body: Marcus called us after furnace line 2 was down for 3 days. Failed blower bearing, no warning, rush parts and overtime. He estimates the outage cost well into six figures in lost shipments. Wants to know if vibration and thermal sensing could have flagged it. Agreed to a plant walk-through and sensor survey.

title: Discovery notes: current maintenance setup
body: Kilnbrook is on calendar-based PM plus operator rounds. No condition monitoring on furnace blowers, pumps or the hydraulic presses. Three furnace lines, about 40 critical assets. Marcus is the pain owner but needs finance sign-off over $250K. Competing priority: a MES upgrade is on the capital list.

title: Plant walk-through and sensor survey
body: Walked all three furnace lines and the machining cell with Marcus and Tobias. Mapped about 40 assets for sensors. Tobias flagged that the furnace area sits on a segmented OT network and wants all data kept on-prem or through a one-way gateway. We agreed a read-only gateway design is workable. Needs a written network architecture doc.

title: Sent network architecture and security overview
body: Sent Tobias the gateway reference design, data flow diagram and our patching policy. Confirmed no inbound connections to the plant network. He will review with his team and come back with questions.

title: Follow-up with OT on gateway questions
body: Tobias is okay with the one-way gateway but wants the firewall rules reviewed by his vendor. Asked about sensor battery life on wireless units, we said about 3 years. No blockers from IT as long as the vendor review passes.

title: Finance request for payback math
body: Renata emailed asking for payback math measured against last year's downtime costs before she will support the $310K. She is skeptical that predictive tools deliver on the promised savings. Replied that we will build a model from Kilnbrook's own downtime data and walk her through assumptions.

title: Marcus shared downtime logs
body: Marcus sent 12 months of downtime logs for the furnace lines and presses. Roughly 14 unplanned stops, with the line 2 outage as the largest. Maintenance labor and expedite costs are included but scrap cost is missing. Asked him to pull scrap figures too.

title: Build payback model before executive presentation
body: Build the payback model from the downtime logs: avoided outage hours, labor, expedite and scrap, with conservative and base cases. Include a sensitivity table for Renata. Review with Marcus a day before the presentation.

title: Executive presentation: predictive maintenance business case
body: Present the plan to Renata, Marcus and plant leadership. Cover the payback model, the pilot scope on furnace line 2, and the gateway design. Expect finance pushback on the savings assumptions.

title: Pilot kickoff on corrugator lines 1 and 2
body: Onsite kickoff with Delphine and her maintenance leads. Sensors going on the two corrugators, focusing on the bearing and drive motor vibration. Baseline unplanned downtime is around 9% of scheduled hours on these lines. Agreed on a six-week pilot with a readout at the end.

title: Mid-pilot check-in
body: Delphine says the dashboards are being used on every shift. First alert flagged a gearbox running hot on line 2, maintenance swapped it during a planned stop. Her concern is that alert noise might wear out the night crew. We will tune the thresholds this week.

title: Tune alert thresholds for night shift
body: Cut low-severity alerts on both lines and send Delphine the revised rules before the readout.

title: Pilot readout with plant and COO
body: Presented results. 11 hours of avoided downtime over six weeks across the two lines, with three early warnings that were acted on. Garrett asked about rollout effort at the other three plants and the cost per line. Delphine backed the results. Garrett said he would approve expanding to all four plants.

title: Expansion proposal and rollout plan
body: Sent the four-plant proposal at $128K with a phased install schedule, two plants per quarter. Included the pilot results summary for Garrett's file and the sensor count per plant.

title: Expansion contract sent for signature
body: Garrett approved the numbers and the contract went out to their legal team. Asked for signature within two weeks to hold the install slots for the first two plants.

title: Legal redlines received
body: Marrowfield legal sent redlines. Main items are a cap on data liability, a request for a 30-day exit if uptime SLA is missed, and wording on who owns the sensor data. Delphine thinks these are routine and that Garrett is still on board. Need our legal to review before the call.

title: Prep redline responses with our legal
body: Agree on fallbacks for the liability cap, SLA exit and data ownership clauses before the call with Marrowfield.

title: Redline resolution call
body: Walk through the open contract items with Marrowfield legal and Delphine. Goal is to agree on language and get to signature this week.

title: Discovery call with Lorna
body: Two hydraulic presses caused about 31 hours of unplanned downtime last quarter. She wants a cost-per-hour number before involving finance.

title: Send downtime cost worksheet
body: Send the blank downtime worksheet so Dev can fill in press stoppage hours for the last six months.

title: Lost: budget frozen
body: Lorna said capex is frozen until the new furnace install is done. Asked us to check back in two quarters.

title: Intro reply from Harlan
body: He replied to our outreach after a spindle failure took out a five-axis mill for nine days. Booked a demo slot.

title: Live demo of spindle dashboards
body: Walk through spindle load and temperature alerts using sample data from a similar gear shop.

title: Scoping notes
body: Harlan runs 14 hobbing machines and logs stoppages on paper. Main objection is operator buy-in on tablets.

title: Proposal presentation
body: Present to Harlan and two shift leads, focusing on automatic stoppage capture without operator entry.

title: Exec alignment call
body: Imani agreed gearbox failures are the top risk and wants a three-plant rollout quote. Piotr will validate the data feeds.

title: Pricing review with procurement
body: Review tiered pricing for three plants and discuss a two-year term.

title: Signed order form
body: Piotr returned the signed order for 12 motor sensors on the pelletizer line. Install scheduled with their electricians.

title: Contract sent
body: Sent the contract covering 40 ammonia compressor sensors. Bettina is routing it to legal this week.

title: Follow up on legal redlines
body: Call Bettina to check whether legal has questions on data ownership language.

title: OEE discovery
body: Current OEE is tracked in spreadsheets and about 20 percent off from reality. Bettina wants this tied to the compressor project.

title: Draft OEE scope
body: Write a scope document for three packing lines and send for review.

title: Technical call with Neville
body: Die crashes cost them roughly 60k last year. He wants tonnage signature alerts on the six largest presses.

title: Onsite presentation
body: Present tonnage monitoring results and include Sasha for the ROI discussion.

title: Went with in-house build
body: Neville's team decided to wire their own sensors to the existing PLC. Left door open for analytics later.

title: Intro call
body: Odalys loses a few batches a month to kiln drift. She is skeptical about cost for a company her size.

title: Kiln walkthrough
body: Visit the plant to look at thermocouple wiring and see what data is already available.

title: Sent conveyor case study
body: Sent a short case study on drive monitoring at a small ceramics plant. Odalys asked for a price for four drives.

title: Prepare four-drive quote
body: Build a quote for four drive sensors with a monthly subscription option.

title: Site director review
body: Yvette approved moving forward after seeing seal failure predictions on their sample data. Needs a safety review of wireless sensors.

title: Send hazardous area certifications
body: Send sensor certification documents for Class I Division 2 areas to Cormac.

title: Batch data call
body: Cormac says cycle times vary 12 percent between shifts and nobody knows why. Historian export is possible.

title: Findings presentation
body: Show cycle time variance analysis built from a sample historian export.

title: Verbal yes
body: Gideon gave a verbal yes for tracking on five weld cells. Contract went out right after the call.

title: Check on signature
body: Confirm Gideon received the contract and offer a quick call for any questions.

title: Kickoff confirmation
body: Confirmed the plasma table sensors are installed and sending data. Gideon liked the consumable wear alerts.

title: Discovery with Ingrid
body: Rewinder jams drive most of their 8 percent downtime. She wants root-cause data before the budget cycle next quarter.

title: Request line data sample
body: Ask Ingrid for two weeks of stoppage logs to build a sample analysis.

title: Intro to Rohan
body: Ingrid looped in Rohan, who is interested in bearing monitoring across both mills. No budget yet.

title: Intro meeting with Rohan
body: Cover bearing monitoring options and how they would fit alongside the downtime project.

title: Discovery follow-up with maintenance
body: Philippa said the two main presses lose about 14 hours a month to unplanned stops, mostly hydraulic pump faults. She wants to see how we would flag pressure drift earlier.

title: Solution demo for plant leadership
body: Walk Wendell and the ops team through downtime dashboards using their press data export. Bring a rough ROI model based on the 14 hours a month.

title: Loss confirmation from Wendell
body: Wendell said budget got pulled for a furnace relining project this year and they will go with manual vibration rounds for now. Agreed to check back in two quarters.

title: Discovery call with maintenance
body: Anouk says hydraulic press faults cost them about 14 hours of unplanned downtime a month. Wants to see vibration and pressure trend data on two presses.

title: Send sensor requirements sheet
body: Send the sensor and gateway list so their controls tech can confirm cabinet space.

title: Intro email on trim presses
body: Lucian asked whether the analytics could cover the trim presses too. Replied with a scope outline and offered a call after the first deal moves.

title: Scoping call
body: Thirty minute call to size the trim press add-on with Lucian.

title: Call on dryer failures
body: Two dryer bearing failures last season stopped the line during peak harvest. Calista wants a demo showing early warning on bearing temperature.

title: Platform demo for ops team
body: Demo with Calista and two shift leads using sample dryer data.

title: Lost to in-house build
body: Calista said their IT team will build OEE dashboards on their existing historian. Left the door open for a revisit next year.

title: Exec review with Ephraim
body: Ephraim agreed the fleet rollout is justified at roughly 3% scrap reduction. Needs a security review from IT before signing.

title: Send security questionnaire answers
body: Return completed IT security questionnaire and data flow diagram.

title: Chiller discussion with Kiara
body: Kiara reports mold temperature drift traced to aging chillers. Interested in a smaller scope as a separate budget line.

title: Chiller data walkthrough
body: Review two months of chiller logs with Kiara to size the use case.

title: Contract questions
body: Bartholomew asked about the termination clause and data ownership. Sent revised language to legal.

title: Follow up on redlines
body: Check that their counsel received the revised terms and get a signing date.

title: Pilot wrapped, signed off
body: Pilot caught a motor current anomaly on the extruder before a breakdown. Bartholomew signed the pilot invoice and wants to talk about the full lines.

title: Furnace use case call
body: Tamsin wants earlier warning on burner and lehr belt issues, since a bad batch scraps about 40 tons. Asked for a reference in glass.

title: Technical demo
body: Demo with Tamsin and her controls lead, focused on thermal profile drift.

title: Pilot idea sent
body: Sent a two-machine pilot outline at the request of Tamsin. She will raise it at the next budget meeting.

title: Check budget outcome
body: Call Tamsin to find out whether the pilot made it into the budget.

title: Intro call
body: Joaquin runs a small shop and worries about cost. Main pain is robotic welder downtime about once a month.

title: Send entry pricing
body: Send the small-plant package pricing with a single cell option.

title: Final terms meeting
body: Philomena and procurement reviewed pricing and a three-year term. They asked for a quarterly review clause, which we agreed to.

title: Send final order form
body: Issue the updated order form with the quarterly review clause.

title: Verbal yes
body: Rosalind confirmed budget approval for the loom monitoring rollout. Kickoff is planned for next month.

title: ROI summary sent
body: Sent Matteo a one-page ROI estimate based on his stated 9% downtime on three blow molders. He forwarded it to the owner.

title: Call with owner
body: Join Matteo and the owner to answer questions on installation time and contract length.

title: Discovery call on spindle failures
body: Corinna said three spindle failures last quarter cost about 40 hours of unplanned downtime each. Emeka wants to see vibration data from our sensors on their older Okuma machines.

title: Demo for plant leadership
body: Walk Corinna and Emeka through the downtime dashboard using sample spindle data. Bring the retrofit sensor spec sheet for the older machines.

title: Discovery call on press downtime
body: Fiona said unplanned press stops cost them about 11 hours a month. Wants to know if sensors can be retrofitted on 2000s-era presses without a PLC rewrite.

title: Walk the press floor
body: On-site walkthrough with maintenance leads to pick candidate machines for a sensor survey.

title: Sent OEE benchmark sheet
body: Shared a sample OEE breakdown from a similar filler line. Hollis wants to see capper jam patterns before the group demo.

title: Demo for ops leadership
body: Present downtime dashboard to Hollis and the shift supervisors using their anonymized line data.

title: Inbound from trade show
body: Dalton stopped by the booth. Runs 14 molding presses and tracks downtime on a whiteboard; budget is tight until next quarter.

title: Send intro deck and pricing range
body: Email the small-plant package overview and a ballpark so Dalton can take it to his partner.

title: Contract redline review
body: Saoirse's legal asked to cap data retention at 24 months. We agreed, and she expects sign-off after the plant council meets.

title: Send revised order form
body: Deliver updated order form with the retention clause and onboarding schedule.

title: Loss call with COO
body: Cassius went with the analytics module bundled in their existing automation vendor's contract. Said price was fine but he did not want a second vendor; open to revisiting in a year.
